name: Context rot and positional attention bias. A cluster of related findings rather than one artifact. Named sources: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts (Liu et al., TACL 2024, arXiv:2307.03172), the origin of the U-shaped position curve; Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance (Hong, Troynikov, Huber; Chroma technical report, July 2025), which coined 'context rot' in this sense; Positional Biases Shift as Inputs Approach Context Window Limits (arXiv:2508.07479), the source of the 50%-of-window crossover; Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval (arXiv:2510.05381); Can Small Language Models Use What They Retrieve? An Empirical Study of Retrieval Utilization Across Model Scale (arXiv:2603.11513); The Power of Noise: Redefining Retrieval for RAG Systems (arXiv:2401.14887); Long-Context LLMs Meet RAG (ICLR 2025); Lost in the Middle: An Emergent Property from Information Retrieval Demands in LLMs (arXiv:2510.10276). Related terms: primacy bias, recency bias, LiM effect, needle-in-a-haystack, distractor sensitivity, attention sink.
kind: Research results -- a body of empirical measurements about model behaviour, plus one vendor technical report. Not a standard, library, benchmark suite, service or regulation, although needle-in-a-haystack style evaluations function as informal benchmarks and are widely criticised within this same literature for being too easy.
maturity: Actively moving and not settled. The U-shaped 'lost in the middle' result (2023-24) is well replicated and is now understood to be conditional rather than universal -- the 2025-26 work shows the shape depends on context fill fraction, model family, model scale and task, and at least one paper argues the U-shape is an emergent property of retrieval demands rather than an intrinsic attention artifact. Any design rule taken from this area has a short half-life and should be re-measured against the actual model in use. What IS stable across every study is the direction: more context is not free, degradation begins well below the advertised window, and it is non-uniform in position.
license: Papers are arXiv preprints and conference publications, freely citable. The Chroma context-rot replication toolkit is on GitHub under a permissive licence. Nothing is being adopted as code; the output of this item is numbers and design rules. [uncertain] on the exact licence of the Chroma toolkit repository.
keeps_and_discards: Not an extraction method, but the framing transfers usefully: this literature is about what a MODEL effectively keeps and discards from what it is given, which is the last stage of the same pipeline. The finding is that a model does not attend uniformly -- it effectively discards material in disfavoured positions and material crowded out by distractors, even when that material is unambiguously present and retrievable. The most severe form of this, and the one most relevant to a project targeting small local models: for models at or below roughly 7B parameters, under ORACLE retrieval where the provided passage definitely contains the answer, the reported failure rate to extract the correct answer is 85-100%, with the dominant failure mode being complete disregard of the provided context. That is not partial forgetting; it is the model ignoring the supplied material and answering from parameters. The corollary in the same study is worse for a retrieval-shaped design: adding retrieval context OVERTURNED 42-64% of answers the model had previously got right, and the authors attribute the effect to the PRESENCE of context rather than to its quality. So at small scale, supplying more page content is not merely subject to diminishing returns -- it can be net harmful, and the harm is not fixed by improving what you supply.
structure_preserved: The relevant question here is whether structure in the INPUT helps a model use it, and the literature's answer is partial and suggestive rather than settled. The Chroma work reports that haystack STRUCTURE affects performance non-uniformly -- how the surrounding material is organised changes retrieval reliability independently of length -- and reports counterintuitive interactions where a coherently structured haystack does not straightforwardly beat a shuffled one. What is clearly established is that semantic RELATEDNESS matters: needle-question similarity drives performance, and semantically similar distractors hurt far more than unrelated filler. For a structured emission this argues that a page's near-duplicate sibling content (a listing of twenty similar products, a nav menu of similar links) is the worst possible filler around a target, because it is maximally distractor-like. Deduplicating and collapsing repeated sibling structure is therefore not only a token economy but an accuracy intervention. [uncertain] -- the structure findings are the least replicated part of this literature.
interactive_elements: No direct treatment. The transferable implication concerns how affordances should be emitted: a list of controls is a set of short, mutually similar, low-information-density items, which is exactly the distractor profile the literature identifies as most damaging, and it will typically be positioned before or after the content the model actually needs. That argues for emitting affordances as a compact, clearly delimited block adjacent to the content they belong to rather than as a long flat list at one end of the observation, and for keeping the count bounded. No study measures this directly.
interactive_state_fidelity: Not applicable in the source literature. Indirectly relevant: state annotations are short, highly repetitive tokens (disabled, checked, expanded) attached to many elements, so they inflate the count of near-identical strings in the context, which is the distractor-density pattern. The design implication is to emit state only where it is non-default -- a control with no state markers is implicitly in its default state -- which cuts the repetition sharply at no information cost. This is a concrete, cheap rule derived from the distractor findings rather than from token counting.
layout_awareness: None -- this literature concerns token sequences and attention, and geometry does not enter. It is entirely compatible with a layout-free fold and constrains only what is emitted and in what order. Note that 'position' in this literature means position in the TOKEN SEQUENCE, not position on a page, and conflating the two would be an error.
evaluation_method: Controlled position and length sweeps. The canonical design, from Liu et al. onward, places a target fact (the 'needle') at systematically varied positions within a controlled amount of filler (the 'haystack'), holds the question fixed, and plots accuracy against position and against total length. Later work extends this along axes the original held constant: needle-question lexical and semantic similarity, presence and similarity of distractors, haystack coherence, and -- crucially -- context fill measured as a FRACTION OF THE MODEL'S WINDOW rather than as an absolute token count, which is what surfaced the 50% crossover. The 2508.07479 method defines explicit metrics for primacy, recency and the lost-in-the-middle effect and reads them directly off the position curves rather than inferring them. The main methodological critique, made forcefully inside this literature by the Chroma report, is that standard needle-in-a-haystack evaluations are too easy -- they use lexically distinctive needles in unrelated filler, which is close to a string-matching task -- and that performance on them substantially overstates real-world long-context reliability. Any figure quoted from a plain needle benchmark should be treated as an upper bound.
corpus_size_and_origins: Mostly synthetic by construction, which is appropriate for a controlled study and is a reach limitation nonetheless. Haystacks are assembled from Paul Graham essays, arXiv text, book corpora, Wikipedia and similar English prose; needles are authored by the researchers. Model coverage is the dimension where reach is best: the Chroma report covers 18 models spanning GPT-4.1, Claude Opus 4, Gemini 2.5 and Qwen3 families, and reports the effect present in every model at every input-length increment tested, which is unusually broad. The RAG-side studies use standard QA sets (NaturalQuestions-derived, EN.QA and EN.MC from long-context suites) with retrieved passage sets. Nothing is evaluated on web-page-shaped input -- no study uses a rendered page, a DOM serialisation, an accessibility tree or markdown converted from HTML as its haystack, so every transfer to this project's setting is by analogy. Given that a web page's filler is highly repetitive, template-generated and semantically adjacent to its content, it is arguably a HARDER haystack than English prose, so the published numbers likely flatter the web case rather than the reverse. All English; no CJK or RTL haystack studies located.
reported_precision_recall: The usable numbers, with denominators and sourcing. (1) THE 50% CROSSOVER (arXiv:2508.07479): the lost-in-the-middle effect is strongest when inputs occupy up to 50% of a model's context window; beyond 50% primacy bias weakens significantly while recency bias remains relatively stable, producing a distance-based bias favouring information closer to the END of the input. This is the specific finding the project's framing refers to and it is confirmed -- with the important refinement that it is not that recency INCREASES past 50%, but that primacy FADES while recency holds, so recency becomes dominant by attrition. The same paper notes that positional biases observed in reasoning are largely inherited from retrieval, i.e. the model fails to find the material rather than failing to reason over it. (2) MAGNITUDE OF THE LiM EFFECT: performance degradation of more than 30% has been reported when relevant information moves from the start or end to the middle of the window; denominator is task accuracy on the position-controlled QA setups. (3) DEGRADATION BEGINS FAR BELOW THE WINDOW (arXiv:2510.05381): a large portion of the drop in problem-solving occurs within 7,000 tokens, well below the point at which retrieval scores themselves begin to degrade, and accuracy drops by a larger margin than retrieval score across almost all tasks and lengths -- so the model can still FIND the material while becoming unable to USE it, and 7k tokens is the practically relevant scale, not 128k. (4) SMALL-MODEL RETRIEVAL UTILISATION (arXiv:2603.11513), the most important numbers here for a local-model project: for models at or below roughly 7B, under ORACLE retrieval, failure to extract the correct answer occurs 85-100% of the time, dominated by outright disregard of the context; and adding retrieval context overturns 42-64% of previously-correct answers, an effect driven by the presence of context rather than its quality. (5) OPTIMAL CONTEXT LENGTH SCALES WITH MODEL SIZE (Long-Context LLMs Meet RAG, ICLR 2025): Llama3.1-8B peaks at 16K tokens on both EN.QA and EN.MC, while Llama3.1-70B peaks at 48K on EN.QA and 32K on EN.MC -- so the 8B model's optimum is roughly a third to a half of the 70B model's, and past the peak both decline. (6) DOCUMENT-COUNT INVERTED U: performance follows an inverted-U in the number of retrieved documents, with a strong retriever reaching the peak EARLIER and declining FASTER than a weak one; reported optima cluster at 3-5 and around 10 documents in several studies, with at least one framework peaking at 20. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE PROJECT'S FRAMING: the specific claim that 7-8B models degrade sharply near 20 retrieved documents was NOT located in the literature searched. What IS supported is the inverted-U shape, published optima considerably LOWER than 20 (commonly 3-10), and a token-denominated optimum of about 16K for Llama3.1-8B. The safe design reading is that the practical ceiling is lower than 20 documents, not that it is at 20.
independent_oracle: Yes and unusually clean: the needle is placed by the experimenter, so ground truth is known by construction and does not depend on any judgement shared with the model. For the RAG studies, oracle retrieval conditions (the passage is guaranteed to contain the answer) isolate the utilisation failure from the retrieval failure, which is exactly the right decomposition and is what makes the 85-100% small-model figure interpretable rather than confounded. The weakness is not the oracle but the ecological validity of the haystack, as the Chroma critique makes clear.
evidence_independence: Mixed and the mixture must be kept explicit. The academic papers (Liu et al., arXiv:2508.07479, 2510.05381, 2603.11513, the ICLR RAG work) are independent of the model vendors whose models they test, which is the right kind of independence for this question and is stronger than most evidence in this research set. The Chroma 'Context Rot' report is a VENDOR TECHNICAL REPORT from a vector-database company whose product is retrieval, and its central thesis -- that long context degrades and you should retrieve selectively rather than dump everything in -- is directly aligned with its commercial interest. That does not make it wrong, and it publishes a replication toolkit, which is a genuine mitigating practice; but the framing, the choice of what to measure and the emphasis are vendor-shaped, and it should be cited as a vendor report that offers replication rather than as neutral research. The convergence between the vendor report's direction and the independent academic findings is what makes the overall conclusion trustworthy, not the vendor report alone. Model vendors' own long-context claims (advertised window sizes, needle-benchmark scores) are self-reported marketing and are contradicted by every source in this item.
page_archetype_coverage: Not applicable in the source studies -- no web pages are used. Reasoning by mechanism about which page archetypes will suffer most under these effects: LISTING and COLLECTION pages are the worst case, because their content is many short, mutually similar items, which is the maximal-distractor configuration the literature identifies as most damaging, and because they are long; DOCUMENTATION and ARTICLE pages are the best case, being coherent prose with a single topic and low distractor density; FORUM and thread pages sit in between, with many similar-shaped posts but genuine topical variation; PRODUCT pages combine a dense specification block (high distractor similarity) with unique prose. This predicts that a fold's accuracy will vary by archetype for reasons that have nothing to do with extraction quality, which is a confound worth controlling for in any evaluation. [uncertain] -- inference from mechanism, not measured.
script_and_locale_behaviour: Unexamined and consequential. Every study located is English. Two concrete transfer problems. First, token budgets are not script-invariant: CJK text costs substantially more tokens per character under common BPE tokenisers, so a fixed token budget carries far less content in Chinese or Japanese, and a fixed CONTENT budget crosses the 50%-fill threshold much sooner -- meaning the recency-dominant regime is entered earlier on CJK pages for the same visible amount of material. Second, distractor similarity is measured in embedding space, and embedder quality varies by language, so the distractor effect's magnitude in non-English content is unknown. Any budget default derived from these English measurements should be treated as an upper bound for CJK content. [uncertain] -- no measurement exists.
leaks_outward: Not applicable to the phenomenon, but the design consequence is real: everything placed in the context is disclosed to whatever model reads it, so a budget rule is simultaneously a disclosure rule. The finding that smaller budgets often perform BETTER means, unusually, that the accuracy-optimal choice and the privacy-optimal choice point the same way, which is worth stating because such alignments are rare.
mechanism_detectability: Not applicable -- this concerns model behaviour, not page observation. No page can detect how a model attends to content derived from it.
countermeasures: The literature's own mitigations, in rough order of evidential support. (1) SUPPLY LESS. Every study supports this and several show it improves accuracy outright. (2) POSITION THE HIGH-VALUE MATERIAL AT THE END when the input is long, since past 50% fill the bias is distance-based toward the end; position it at the START or END but never the middle when the input is short, since below 50% fill the U-shape dominates. (3) REMOVE SEMANTICALLY SIMILAR DISTRACTORS in preference to removing unrelated filler -- the similarity of the distractor matters more than its volume, so deduplicating near-identical sibling content buys more accuracy per token than trimming unrelated material. (4) KEEP THE TOTAL WELL BELOW THE WINDOW, and specifically below the 7k-token scale at which problem-solving degradation is already substantial, rather than below the advertised limit. (5) FOR SMALL MODELS, RECONSIDER SUPPLYING CONTEXT AT ALL for questions the model can answer from parameters, given that context presence overturned 42-64% of previously-correct answers -- the practical form of this is to make context supply explicit and scoped rather than automatic. (6) Reordering and re-ranking so the most relevant material occupies favoured positions, which is standard RAG practice and which the position findings justify.
measured_fidelity_cost: Measured in the right direction and rarely in the right units. The clean statements: moving relevant material to the middle costs more than 30% of accuracy; exceeding the model-specific optimum context length costs accuracy monotonically thereafter (Llama3.1-8B declining past 16K); adding context to a small model costs 42-64% of its previously-correct answers. Against controls of, respectively, edge placement, shorter context, and no context. What is NOT measured is the cost of the mitigations -- nobody reports how much genuinely-needed content is lost by trimming to a small budget, because the studies vary length by adding filler rather than by removing signal. That asymmetry matters: these papers show that adding NOISE hurts, and do not show that removing SIGNAL is free. A project trimming a real page is doing the second thing, and the literature does not license the inference.
gate_state_at_capture: Not applicable in the source literature. The transferable point is that a consent overlay, paywall notice or login prompt injected into an observation is a large block of semantically-coherent, instruction-shaped text sitting at a favoured position, and is therefore an unusually effective distractor -- so gated captures degrade model performance for a reason unrelated to the content being gated. That is another argument for detecting and recording gate state rather than letting the banner text flow into the observation unlabelled.
determinism: The phenomenon is a statistical property of model behaviour, so individual generations are non-deterministic under sampling and the measured curves are averages over many trials. Greedy decoding at temperature zero makes a single generation reproducible for a fixed model and fixed input, but does not make the position effect go away -- it is a property of attention, not of sampling. Practical consequence for this project's measurement discipline: any comparison of two emission orders or two budgets must be averaged over many trials, exactly as the ACI literature (item 27) requires for agent comparisons, and single-run A/B results are noise.
determinism_across_versions: Poor, and this is the most important caveat on every number in this item. Position bias is a property of a specific model checkpoint: it varies by family, by scale, by training recipe, by positional-encoding scheme and by context-extension method, and at least one study reports that the direction of bias varies by model family with some models showing primacy-dominant behaviour contrasting with the U-shape seen at 13B-and-above scales. Hosted models change silently behind stable API names. Therefore a budget or ordering rule justified by a published curve is justified only for the model that curve was measured on, and the project MUST measure its own model. The durable, transferable content of this item is the SHAPE of the questions to ask (where is my model's optimum length; where is my model's crossover; how does my model respond to similar distractors) and the METHOD for answering them, not the specific thresholds.
reproducibility: Better than most of this research set at the method level and poor at the result level. Method: the needle-in-a-haystack design is trivial to reimplement, Chroma publishes a replication toolkit, and the haystack corpora are public. Result: the models measured are largely hosted and mutable, several are already superseded, and the specific curves cannot be re-obtained. The right posture is to treat this literature as a source of experimental designs to run locally against the actual model, and to store the resulting curves as a project artifact with the model version pinned -- which for a locally-run GGUF model is entirely achievable and is a genuine reproducibility advantage over the hosted-model studies.
failure_modes: (1) MIDDLE NEGLECT below 50% fill -- material in the centre is effectively unread, costing 30%+ accuracy. (2) PRIMACY COLLAPSE above 50% fill -- material at the start loses its advantage while the end retains it, so an instruction or a schema placed at the top of a long input is progressively ignored as the input grows; this is the failure most likely to bite a design that puts its output contract first and its content after. (3) DISTRACTOR CAPTURE -- semantically similar but wrong material outcompetes the correct material, and similarity matters more than volume. (4) CONTEXT DISREGARD AT SMALL SCALE -- the model answers from parameters and ignores supplied material entirely, 85-100% of the time under oracle retrieval for sub-7B models. (5) CONTEXT-INDUCED REGRESSION -- supplying context flips previously-correct answers to incorrect at 42-64% rates for small models, driven by presence rather than quality. (6) PAST-PEAK DECLINE -- accuracy falls monotonically once the model-specific optimum length is exceeded, with the optimum scaling with model size (16K for an 8B, 32-48K for a 70B). (7) BENCHMARK OVERSTATEMENT -- performance on clean needle benchmarks substantially exceeds performance on realistic material, so a model that passes a haystack test is not thereby shown to be reliable.
failure_visibility: Entirely silent, and this is the property that makes context rot dangerous rather than merely inconvenient. The model produces a fluent, confident answer that omits or contradicts material it was given; there is no error, no warning, no signal that anything was missed. There is no in-band detector. The only available checks are out of band and should be built deliberately: ask the model to cite the address of the material it used and verify the citation resolves to content that supports the answer (which the trie key makes cheap and exact); probe with a known control item planted at a known position and check it is recovered; and compare answers at two budgets, where disagreement indicates the larger budget's extra content changed the outcome and warrants inspection. The first of these is the strongest and is nearly free in this design -- a provenance-carrying projection turns an unverifiable answer into a checkable one.
scale_limits: The binding number is far below the advertised window and this is the item's most practically useful correction. Degradation is measurable from the smallest lengths tested and a large share of problem-solving loss occurs within 7,000 tokens; the model-specific accuracy OPTIMUM for an 8B-class model was measured at about 16K tokens; the position-regime crossover is at 50% of the window; and the advertised window (128K, 1M) has essentially no relationship to the length at which the model remains reliable. For a project running a 7-8B local model, the operative figures are therefore: degradation begins immediately, the optimum is on the order of 16K tokens TOTAL for a whole session, the regime change happens at half the window, and the small-model context-utilisation failures make the effective useful budget smaller still.
delta_cost_model: Not a delta-structured phenomenon, but it imposes a hard constraint on any delta-driven emission and the constraint deserves to be stated in these terms. A change-driven interface emits only what changed, which is the ideal shape for keeping total context low -- but the TRANSCRIPT accumulates, so a session's context grows monotonically with the number of interactions regardless of how small each delta is. That growth is what falls outside any per-change cost model: the per-emission cost is O(delta), and the per-session cost is the sum of all deltas plus all prior observations, which crosses the 50% crossover and then the model's optimum after a bounded number of steps no matter how well each step is bounded. Named exclusions from any O(delta) claim about model-facing cost: (1) the accumulating transcript, which is the dominant term and is unbounded in session length; (2) the initial full observation, which is O(page); (3) any re-emission forced by the model losing track of earlier material -- which the position findings predict WILL happen, since early material loses its primacy advantage as the context fills, so a well-behaved long session must periodically RE-STATE material it already sent, and that re-statement is O(state) rather than O(delta); (4) instructions and schema, which must be re-anchored near the end as the input grows rather than stated once at the start. Point (3) is the important one and is rarely acknowledged: position bias means a long session cannot rely on anything it said early, so incremental emission has an unavoidable periodic O(state) refresh cost.
reanchoring_stability: Not applicable to node identity, but there is a direct analogue worth naming: the model's ability to re-anchor to material it was given earlier degrades as the context fills, because primacy fades past 50%. So a reference the model could resolve at step three may be unresolvable at step twenty even though the text is still present verbatim. The mitigation is the same as the delta one -- periodically restate the material the model must keep resolving, and prefer explicit addresses over 'as mentioned above', since an address can be re-fetched and a backreference cannot.
adversarial_exposure: This literature is not about adversarial content and its findings are nonetheless directly relevant to injection risk, in a way that cuts both ways. FAVOURABLE: the same degradation that makes a model ignore relevant material also makes it ignore injected material in disfavoured positions, so a payload buried mid-context in a long input is less likely to take effect. UNFAVOURABLE and more important: the position findings hand an attacker an optimal placement rule. Past 50% fill the bias is distance-based toward the END, so an injection placed at the end of a long observation sits in the most-attended position, and page content that appears late in document order lands there by default -- footers, comment threads, appended sections and lazily-loaded content are precisely the untrusted regions and precisely the favoured position. Below 50% fill the U-shape favours both ends, and the beginning of a page is where a hostile ad or overlay sits. Additionally, the distractor findings mean an attacker can degrade the model's use of legitimate content simply by adding semantically similar noise, without any prompt injection at all -- a purely quantitative attack on comprehension. The design responses are concrete: never let untrusted page content occupy the final position by default (place the task restatement or the output contract there instead), bound the amount of any single untrusted region, and treat the ordering of the emission as a security-relevant decision rather than a formatting one. This interacts with the layout-blind ceiling from item 28: a fold that cannot see concealment is relying on position and volume discipline as a partial compensating control, and position discipline is therefore load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
provenance_carrying: Not a property of the phenomenon, but the phenomenon makes provenance operationally necessary. Because failure is silent, the only practical detector is verifiable citation: if every emitted block carries its address and the model is required to cite the addresses it used, an answer becomes checkable against the store. That converts an invisible failure into a testable one and is the strongest argument in this item for inline, model-visible provenance rather than side-channel metadata. It also has a safety payoff: an answer citing an address in a hidden or untrusted region is detectable as such, which is a partial defence that costs only the citation tokens.
roundtrip_safety: Not applicable as serialisation. An analogous check exists and is worth adopting: emit, ask the model to reproduce or enumerate what it was given, and compare against what was actually emitted. Disagreement measures effective rather than nominal delivery, and it is an oracle-free measurement of how much of the observation the model actually took in. Nobody in this literature frames it this way but it is a straightforward instrument for setting a budget empirically on the project's own model rather than importing someone else's threshold.
token_budget_and_ordering: This is the item's whole purpose and the guidance is now specific enough to implement. DEFAULT BUDGET. Three independent anchors converge on a small number: substantial problem-solving degradation is already present within 7,000 tokens; the measured optimum for an 8B-class model is about 16,000 tokens; and the positional regime changes at 50% of the window. For a 7-8B local model with a typical 8K-32K practical window, the operative rule is to keep the TOTAL SESSION context under 50% of the window, and to keep any single observation to a small fraction of that so a multi-step session stays under the threshold -- concretely, if the expected interaction depth is D steps, the per-emission budget should be roughly (0.5 x window) / D, minus room for instructions and the transcript. For a 32K window and ten expected expansions that is on the order of 1,500 tokens per emission, which is far smaller than any published downsampler's output and is the number a text(budget=...) default should be built around. Round down rather than up: every study in this item found that less was better than more, and the small-model utilisation findings (context presence overturning 42-64% of correct answers) mean a large observation can be actively harmful rather than merely wasteful. ORDERING, which is an output contract and not a formatting preference. Below 50% fill, both ends are favoured and the middle is neglected by 30%+, so the highest-value content goes at the start OR the end and never the middle; above 50% fill, primacy fades and recency holds, so the END is the only reliably-attended position. Since a session's fill only ever increases, the robust rule is: PUT THE HIGHEST-VALUE MATERIAL LAST. In practice that means the emission order should be (a) provenance and structural frame first, (b) bulk content and child lists in the middle, (c) the specific node or content the model asked for, and the output contract or task restatement, LAST -- the inverse of the natural document order, and the inverse of what a human-facing rendering would do. Two further rules with direct evidential support: prefer removing SEMANTICALLY SIMILAR content over removing unrelated content when trimming, because distractor similarity dominates distractor volume, which makes collapsing repeated sibling structure the single highest-value trim; and never leave untrusted page content in the final position, both because it is the most-attended slot and because it is the slot an attacker would choose. Finally, RE-STATE PERIODICALLY: because primacy fades as fill grows, material stated early in a long session becomes effectively unavailable, so a long interaction needs a periodic restatement of the persistent frame near the end of the context, which is an O(state) cost that any incremental design must budget for explicitly.
representation_cost: The relevant cost is not tokens but ACCURACY PER TOKEN, and this literature's contribution is showing the curve is non-monotonic: accuracy rises with content up to a model-specific optimum and falls thereafter, so tokens past the optimum have negative value. Measured optima: about 16K tokens for Llama3.1-8B, 32-48K for Llama3.1-70B; document-count optima commonly 3-10 with an inverted-U shape that peaks EARLIER and falls FASTER when the retriever is strong -- a counterintuitive and important detail, because it means improving the projection's precision should be accompanied by REDUCING its volume, not by keeping it constant. What is lost per token saved is not measured anywhere in this literature, because these studies vary length by adding filler rather than by removing signal; that inference has to come from the project's own affordance-recall measurement.
what_could_be_adopted: Six things, all design rules rather than code. (1) THE PUT-HIGH-VALUE-CONTENT-LAST ORDERING RULE, justified by the 50% crossover and robust because session fill only increases. This is the concrete output contract the project asked for. (2) A PER-EMISSION BUDGET DERIVED FROM EXPECTED SESSION DEPTH rather than from the window size -- (0.5 x window)/steps -- which is a different and much smaller number than 'what fits'. (3) SIMILARITY-AWARE TRIMMING: collapse near-identical sibling content first, because distractor similarity hurts more than distractor volume; this happens to be the same operation structural consolidation performs (item 29), so one mechanism serves both the token budget and the accuracy goal. (4) VERIFIABLE CITATION AS THE FAILURE DETECTOR: require address citations, check they resolve, since context rot is otherwise entirely silent and the trie key makes the check exact. (5) PERIODIC RESTATEMENT of the persistent frame near the end of a long session, budgeted for explicitly as an exception to O(delta). (6) MEASURE THE LOCAL MODEL'S OWN CURVES using the published experimental design -- position sweep, length sweep, distractor-similarity sweep -- and store them as a pinned artifact, since a locally-run model is one of the few settings where these curves can be measured once and stay valid. Explicitly NOT to be adopted: any specific published threshold as a constant, since bias direction and magnitude vary by model family and scale and the hosted models measured are already superseded; and the assumption that trimming is free, which these studies do not establish because they never remove signal.
constraint_violation_ledger: structure_agnosticism: ADOPTABLE AS-IS. Every rule derived here is about ORDER and VOLUME of emission, not about which page regions mean what. Placing high-value content last, bounding the budget, and collapsing near-identical siblings are all structural or positional operations that name no region. The one boundary case is 'high-value content', which must be defined as 'the content the model explicitly requested by address' rather than 'the content a relevance model judged important' -- with the first definition the rule is constraint-clean, with the second it smuggles in a classifier. That distinction should be written into the implementation. no_layout_in_the_fold: ADOPTABLE AS-IS; position here means position in the token sequence and geometry never enters. o_delta: ADOPTABLE AS-IS AS A CONSTRAINT, WITH ONE MAJOR NAMED EXCEPTION IT IMPOSES. This literature does not violate O(delta); it reveals that O(delta) emission is insufficient, because the accumulating transcript and the fading of primacy mean a long session must periodically re-state material it already sent, at O(state) cost. That periodic refresh is the exception that must be published alongside any O(delta) claim about model-facing cost, and it is one this project would otherwise miss entirely. no_mocks: ADOPTABLE AS-IS -- these are measurements of real models on real inputs, and the recommended local replication runs the project's actual model with no stub anywhere. legal_basis_and_pii_posture: Not a data-processing mechanism, but it has one clear implication for the project's posture. Because accuracy peaks at a modest context length and declines thereafter, the accuracy-optimal amount of page content to place in a model's context is SMALLER than the maximum, which means data minimisation is not in tension with performance here -- it is aligned with it. For a hosted model, every token of page content in the context is a disclosure of third-party content, potentially including personal data, so a tight budget is simultaneously a lawful-basis and a performance argument. For the project's local model, the disclosure boundary is internal and the argument is purely about accuracy. Transcripts, if retained, are stored page content and inherit the same retention and erasure obligations as captures.
